outcome: A dispatch on a native CLI lane journals one bounded, redacted record per worker turn as it happens, carrying what the worker said and which tools it called, and its tool results are keyed to the turn they belong to, so a native-lane dispatch can be read back and profiled turn by turn exactly as an HTTP-lane dispatch can today.

acceptance.text: The native event reader recognises the worker-turn events of each native CLI family instead of discarding them: for the Claude family the stream-json assistant and user events, for the Codex family the completed agent-message and tool-call items. From each it derives one turn projection: a turn ordinal that advances at every assistant turn boundary, and an ordered list of bounded parts, each with a kind (text, reasoning where the CLI emits it, tool call with the tool name and its bounded input, tool result reference), total bytes, omitted bytes, redacted bytes and a bounded head and tail. The projection is taken while the line's bytes are live, before the reader clears them, and after the existing secret-leak scan. The built fake native CLI emits these events so the behaviour is exercised against a real child process. Anchor: internal/driver/native_linux_test.go and internal/driver/testdata/nativecontinuation/main.go.

Tool results on a native lane are keyed to the turn they belong to. Today the broker reads its turn from a counter that the Claude family advances only on the final result event, so every tool result of a dispatch lands on turn 0 and a whole dispatch journals one or two tool_result_observed rows. After this slice a Claude-family dispatch with N tool-calling turns journals tool_result_observed rows on N distinct turns, in order, and the Codex family keeps its per-turn keying. The turn count that usage records and economy guards consume keeps its present meaning: if the observation turn ordinal differs from it, the two are separately named values and the design submission says so. Anchor: internal/driver/tool_result_observation_test.go and internal/driver/native_linux_test.go.

Each turn projection is journaled as one event of a new named kind with its own schema version, carrying the same identity the tool-result event carries (run, track, slice, role, responsibility, attempt, epoch, try, work and effect identifiers, turn, part and parts, dropped events) so a reader can join a worker turn to its tool results by identity and turn. It is written through the same per-dispatch hook path, invocation field and non-blocking bounded observer that tool-result observation uses, stays under the journal's event byte bound in the worst case by the same exact-accounting split into named parts, and replays through the journal's existing window, events-after and observer-cursor reads. Anchor: internal/runtime/tool_result_observation_test.go and internal/journal/tool_result_events_test.go.

Bounds and redaction are the existing ones, applied at the emit seam. Every head and tail is bounded by declared constants, omitted bytes are named rather than silently dropped, and every secret bound for the dispatch (the capability, the capture bearer and the credential fragments) is replaced before any byte reaches the hook, by the same longest-first replacement that cannot grow a span past its bound. A turn whose event cannot be decoded, or whose shape the reader does not recognise, is counted in dropped events and never retained raw. Anchor: internal/driver/tool_result_observation_test.go.

Observation never changes delivery. A hook that fails, blocks or is absent, an observer queue that overflows, and an unrecognised or malformed worker-turn event each leave the dispatch result, the handoff, the receipt, the usage record and the byte-budget accounting identical to an unobserved dispatch, with drops counted loudly. The existing refusals in the reader keep their precedence: a secret leak still refuses first, the cumulative output budget still refuses at the same byte, and a disallowed Codex item type is still refused. Automation dispatches stay unobserved. Anchor: internal/driver/tool_result_observation_test.go and internal/driver/native_linux_test.go.

docs/run.md documents the worker-turn event beside the existing telemetry notes: its kind and schema version, its fields, its bounds, what is redacted, that HTTP lanes and native lanes now both journal per turn, and how to profile a dispatch by turn from the journal. Anchor: docs/run.md.

constraints: Extend the one observation mechanism; do not build a second. internal/driver/tool_result_observation.go owns projection, bounds, redaction, part splitting and the non-blocking observer, and internal/runtime/tool_result_observation.go owns the journaling hook. The worker-turn record reuses those seams (projectToolResult's head-then-tail geometry, redactToolResultSpan, splitToolResultParts' exact accounting, toolResultObserver, Invocation hook threading from internal/runtime/dispatch.go). Introduce new representation only where a worker turn cannot truthfully use the tool-result shape, and keep the tool_result_observed kind and its sworn.tool-result-turn/v1 schema byte-compatible for existing readers.

The native reader zeroes every line after it is accepted (scanNativeEvents in internal/driver/native_linux.go) and scans for capability and secret leaks before accept runs. Both stay. No raw line, content block or tool input is retained beyond the bounded, redacted projection, in memory or on disk.

The reader's strictness toward authority-bearing events does not loosen. The init event's closed-object validation, session identity capture, result and usage capture, the CLI error result capture from #314, and the Codex disallowed-item refusals are unchanged. Worker-turn events are observation input only: tolerant to unknown fields, never a source of authority, identity, usage or refusal.

The native argv is pinned by tests and stays as it is. This slice does not add --include-partial-messages or any other flag: token-level deltas multiply stream bytes against the manifest-governed output budget and are deferred with the live stream's follow-up, not smuggled in here.

No journal schema migration. The event is a new kind in the existing events table under the existing event byte bound. It carries the event association fields existing projections read, so the cockpit's metadata-only evidence list keeps working without reading the new body.

This slice adds no presentation. The cockpit projector, browser board, TUI and telemetry export do not render or export the new event here; S2 and S3 consume it. internal/cockpit, internal/tui and internal/observe are in scope only for fixtures and regressions the change forces.

Every listed check is a host check: contained implementers and verifiers consume engine-bound host evidence and never attempt nested containment or claim to have executed these commands. Each long process suite runs once per candidate in the phase order the engine defines.

This release changes no roster, model selection, budget, timeout, retry cap or fallback behaviour, and no gate, verdict or authority path. A worker-turn record is unverified observation: never a check result, a Lead decision, a Verifier verdict or evidence of correctness.
The broad supporting package scope admits only this promised mechanism and its affected regression fixtures, adapters and documentation. It grants no unrelated refactor.

Known contained-workspace facts, not defects of this slice: cmd/sworn's TestTUIActionDriveSurvivesActionReturn fails in the sandbox with CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE and prints roughly 90 KB of DEBUG output; it passes on the host. Do not chase it and do not run it in the workspace. internal/runtime exceeds Go's implicit 10-minute package deadline in the sandbox; pass -timeout=20m on your own package runs. The sandbox shell is dash without `which`. Never build a binary into the workspace root: an out-of-scope file at the root makes checkpoint capture refuse with CHECKPOINT_SCOPE_VIOLATION and fences the workspace; build into a temporary directory.

internal/protocol is the embedded protocol package. This slice needs no change to its receipt vocabulary, operation assets or pinned digests; if a design appears to need one, report it rather than re-pinning the bundle.
